name: Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor – Checkout, Payment & Order Failure Monitor
author: Web Plura

sections.description:
Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor gives WooCommerce store admins a local view of payment gateway readiness, checkout setup, failed-order pressure, pending-order patterns, and report history.

The plugin focuses on practical local checks that a store owner or agency can run from wp-admin:

  • Enabled gateway inventory.
  • Gateway provider and plugin-version readiness matrix.
  • Checkout page surface checks for assignment, publishing, block/shortcode presence, and HTTPS.
  • Failed and pending payment trend review.
  • Aged pending and paid-but-pending diagnostics by gateway.
  • Webhook URL and gateway configuration checklist.
  • Currency mismatch warnings where locally detectable.
  • Test payment readiness checklist.
  • Manual gateway test log stored locally in WordPress.
  • WordPress Site Health checks for recent scan and gateway readiness.
  • Transparent local gateway risk score.
  • Local report history, printable summaries, history CSV/JSON exports, issue CSV export, and gateway readiness CSV export.

All features described in this readme are included in the WordPress.org package and work locally after activation. The plugin does not require an external account or remote payment monitoring service. It does not transmit payment monitoring data externally.

Product page: https://wplura.com/products/web-plura-payment-gateway-monitor
Terms: https://wplura.com/terms
Privacy: https://wplura.com/privacy

Optional Web Plura Services

The WordPress.org package is fully functional for the local payment monitoring features listed above. Separately installed or hosted Web Plura services may offer account-backed support, hosted operations, or cross-site workflows. Those services do not unlock the local gateway checks, manual test log, reports, print views, exports, settings, or Site Health signals included in this plugin.

External Services

This free plugin does not connect to external services and does not transmit payment monitoring data externally.

The plugin reads local WooCommerce configuration, payment gateway settings visible to WordPress, and recent order-status patterns. Reports are viewed or exported manually by the administrator. Payment provider secrets, full customer payment details, order notes, and external gateway logs are not collected by this plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the web-plura-payment-gateway-monitor folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Web Plura Payment Gateway Monitor in wp-admin.
  4. Run a local scan.
sections.faq:
Does this require WooCommerce?

Yes. It is built for WooCommerce payment gateway checks.

Does this require an external account?

No. The local dashboard, local scan, checklist, score, reports, printable summaries, manual test log, CSV exports, and JSON exports work without an external account or remote payment monitoring service.

What problems does it look for?

It helps review failed payment pressure, pending payment patterns, paid-but-pending signals, enabled gateways, provider/plugin readiness, checkout page readiness, webhook readiness, currency mismatch signals where available, conditional payment plugin awareness, and basic test-payment readiness.

What does the plugin send externally?

Nothing. This free plugin keeps payment monitoring scans and report history inside WordPress.

Are any listed local features restricted?

No. The WordPress.org package includes the local gateway checks, payment trend review, webhook checklist, manual gateway test log, Site Health checks, local risk score, local report history, printable summaries, CSV exports, and JSON exports described here. Scan size and retention settings are local performance and storage safeguards, not feature restrictions.

Does it store payment provider secrets?

No. The plugin does not store Stripe, PayPal, or other gateway secret keys.
